input.quote: f) IBM agrees that, for a period of [*] years from the Effective Date of this Agreement, it will not in any way solicit for employment any Transferred Employees without the prior written consent of MSL; provided, however, that the foregoing will not restrict or prevent IBM from a) employing any such person who contacts IBM on his or her own initiative without any solicitation or encouragement from IBM or b) by using general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms, hiring any person who responds thereto, provided that IBM does not direct or encourage such independent search firms to solicit such Transferred Employees.
input.rationale: Section 9.0(f) is the only hiring restriction in the Agreement (16.7 and 5.2 contain no personnel-hiring constraints), and it binds IBM. It sits at the playbook fallback on all material terms: (i) scope is narrow — limited to the finite, listed group of "Transferred Employees" (the ex-IBM staff who moved to MSL to perform the work), not all MSL personnel; (ii) it is a solicitation-only restriction with no "no-hire" — IBM may in fact hire Transferred Employees who approach it or respond to advertising; and (iii) both required carve-outs are present, for unsolicited approaches on the individual's own initiative and for general employment advertising/communications and independent search firms. Two points short of the preferred position are noted rather than flagged: the covenant is one-way rather than mutual, and the duration is redacted ("[*] years") and runs from the Effective Date rather than from the end of an individual's involvement. We should confirm on the unredacted copy that the period does not exceed 24 months (walk-away); as drafted from a fixed Effective Date rather than a rolling engagement date, the restriction is self-limiting and does not warrant a redline.
